claim.value: A publication difference can support an effect of the change when random assignment is valid, follow-up is comparable and outcome capture is reliable.
claim.scope: Conditional causal support, not guaranteed causal certainty or a report that these conditions hold.

provenance.rationale: P020 states the conditional causal inference. P026–P027 bound its interpretation when evidence is sparse or validity checks fail.

signal_basis.value: Compare the proportion of eligible accounts reaching a traceable first publication under the change versus the current flow, using valid random assignment, comparable follow-up and reliable outcome capture.
signal_basis.scope: The predefined observation window covers intended roster opportunities. The publication difference is assumed observed for this judgment; the mapping reports no completed findings. Linkage and capture comparability must be verified.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply the comparison, assignment procedure, outcome, observation window, measurement safeguards and prospective status.
The claim is supported under its stated prerequisites; no additional unresolved empirical relation is needed to license this qualified inference.

rationale: With the stipulated validity conditions satisfied, a randomized comparison of publication outcomes can provide causal evidence about the change. The claim says that a difference can support an effect, preserving the distinction between evidence and certainty. It does not infer customer improvement from documentary continuity alone.
uncertainty: No effect magnitude, sample size or statistical precision is supplied. These omissions limit the strength of any actual result but do not defeat the qualified warrant. The mapping explicitly requires retaining uncertainty or stopping causal interpretation when evidence is too sparse or checks fail.
